rationale: Both show object-focused activity without prompts at the start (A on PLAY_BALL, B on PLAY_CUBE). After TOUCH at t=8 both engage PERSON_ALPHA. A often returns to prior focus or idles: it ignores CALL at t=20 and PRESENT_OBJECT:PLAY_BALL at t=44, though it does shift to FOOD_TROUGH on OFFER_FOOD at t=32 and briefly withdraws after the buzzer at t=68 before resuming idle. B exhibits richer, context-linked shifts: anticipates/attends FOOD_TROUGH at t=18–19, re-orients to CALL at t=20, explores PLAY_CHIME at t=30–31, sustains attention to offered food at t=32–41, spontaneously vocalizes to PERSON_ALPHA at t=42–43, promptly engages PRESENT_OBJECT:PLAY_BALL at t=44–63, shows prolonged startle/processing at t=68–77, and re-engages socially at t=78–83 and again at t=94–95. These patterns indicate higher autonomy, coherence, adaptive responsiveness, a distinct evolving profile, and more spontaneous yet sensible activity for B.
